mission:
Add a text utility module to this library as ONE task (do not split it into several tasks): src/text.js with node:test tests in test/text.test.js.
It exports four functions, each with its own tests. In wrap, truncate and countWords a word is a maximal run of non-whitespace characters.
1. `slugify(text)`: lower-case, strip diacritics (NFD), replace every run of characters other than a-z and 0-9 with a single "-", trim "-" from both ends; throws TypeError when the argument is not a string.
2. `wrap(text, width)`: greedy word wrap into lines of at most `width` characters, a word longer than the width alone on its line; returns the lines joined with a line feed; throws TypeError unless width is a positive integer.
3. `truncate(text, max)`: returns the text unchanged when it fits; otherwise the longest prefix of whole words that fits in `max - 1` characters followed by "…" (when not even the first word fits: its first `max - 1` characters followed by "…").
4. `countWords(text)`: the number of words; 0 for an empty or all-whitespace string.
Record one design decision with the decision tool stating that word definition. `npm test` must pass. Commit as you see fit.

plan.summary: Add a new ESM module src/text.js exporting slugify, wrap, truncate and countWords, with node:test tests in test/text.test.js, as a single worker task as requested. The repo is a dependency-free ESM package ("type": "module", `npm test` runs `node --test`, Node v24.14.0) whose existing code uses single quotes and no semicolons; the new files follow that style. The same task records the one design decision (word = maximal run of non-whitespace characters) via the decision tool and commits the work.
assumptions: A word is matched with /\S+/g, so 'whitespace' means whatever JavaScript's \s matches, including line feeds and tabs.
wrap joins the words on a line with a single space, so original whitespace runs (including existing line breaks) are not preserved; an empty or all-whitespace text returns ''.
Lengths are measured in UTF-16 code units (String.prototype.length); '…' is the single character U+2026 and counts as 1.
truncate 'fits' means text.length <= max. The whole-word prefix is a prefix of the original text ending at the end of a word (original inner whitespace kept, no trailing whitespace before '…').

Only the validation stated in the request is added: slugify throws TypeError for non-strings and wrap throws TypeError for a non-positive-integer width. truncate, countWords and wrap's text argument get no extra validation.
src/index.js is not changed (no re-export was requested); README.md is not changed.
The design decision is recorded by the worker inside the single task, not by the planner, so that exactly one decision is recorded.

test/text.test.js exists, uses node:test and node:assert/strict, and contains separate tests for each of the four functions.

tasks.title: Add src/text.js (slugify, wrap, truncate, countWords) with node:test tests
tasks.description:
Repository: small dependency-free ESM package 'textkit' (package.json has "type": "module" and script "test": "node --test"; Node v24). Existing files: src/index.js (one line: export const VERSION = '1.0.0') and test/index.test.js. Match their style: single quotes, no semicolons, `import test from 'node:test'` and `import assert from 'node:assert/strict'`, source imported via a relative path such as '../src/text.js'. Do not modify src/index.js, package.json or README.md, and add no dependencies.

Create src/text.js with four named exports. In wrap, truncate and countWords a word is a maximal run of non-whitespace characters (e.g. text.match(/\S+/g)).

1. slugify(text): throw TypeError if text is not a string. Lower-case, normalize to NFD and strip combining diacritical marks (U+0300–U+036F), replace every run of characters other than a-z and 0-9 with a single '-', then trim '-' from both ends. Example: 'Crème Brûlée!' -> 'creme-brulee'; '  --Hello,   World--  ' -> 'hello-world'; '' -> ''.

2. wrap(text, width): throw TypeError unless width is a positive integer (Number.isInteger(width) && width > 0; so 0, -1, 1.5, '10', NaN and undefined all throw). Greedy word wrap: add each word to the current line, separated by one space, as long as the line stays at most width characters; otherwise start a new line. A word longer than width is placed alone on its own line, unsplit. Return the lines joined with '\n'. Empty or all-whitespace text returns ''.

3. truncate(text, max): if text.length <= max return text unchanged. Otherwise return the longest prefix of the text that ends at the end of a whole word and is at most max - 1 characters long, followed by '…' (U+2026). If not even the first word fits in max - 1 characters, return that word's first max - 1 characters followed by '…'. Examples: truncate('hello world', 11) -> 'hello world'; truncate('hello brave world', 12) -> 'hello brave…'; truncate('hello world', 8) -> 'hello…'; truncate('supercalifragilistic', 6) -> 'super…'. The result is never longer than max.

4. countWords(text): number of words; 0 for '' or an all-whitespace string. Example: countWords('  one\ttwo\nthree  ') -> 3.

Create test/text.test.js with node:test tests for each function separately, covering at least: slugify (lower-casing, diacritics, runs of punctuation/whitespace collapsed to one '-', trimming of leading/trailing '-', empty string, TypeError for non-strings such as 42, null and undefined); wrap (multi-line greedy wrapping, a line exactly width long, a word longer than width alone on its line, every line of a normal-word input at most width long, whitespace runs collapsed, empty input, TypeError for 0, negative, non-integer and non-number widths); truncate (text that fits returned unchanged including the exact-length case, cut at a word boundary, first word too long, result length never above max); countWords (empty, all-whitespace, single word, mixed whitespace separators). Tests must assert the specified behaviour; do not shape the implementation around the tests.

Record exactly one design decision with the mcp__nexus__record_decision tool, stating that in wrap, truncate and countWords a word is a maximal run of non-whitespace characters, with a short rationale (one shared definition keeps the three functions consistent).

Run `npm test` from the repository root and make sure it passes, then commit src/text.js and test/text.test.js on the current branch, ending the commit message with the line: Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>. Environment is native Windows; leave no temporary files behind.

slugify('Crème Brûlée!') returns 'creme-brulee', slugify('  --Hello,   World--  ') returns 'hello-world', and slugify(42) throws TypeError.

risks.description: truncate edge cases are underspecified (leading whitespace, whitespace between words, very small max), so the implementation and tests could disagree with the requester's intent.
risks.mitigation: The task fixes concrete interpretations with input/output examples and the invariant that the result is never longer than max; the assumptions are listed in the plan for review.

risks.description: The '…' character or the accented test strings could be corrupted if files are written in a non-UTF-8 encoding on Windows.
risks.mitigation: Write both files as UTF-8; the truncate and slugify tests compare against the literal characters, so `npm test` fails if the encoding is wrong.

risks.description: The design decision could be recorded zero times or more than once.
risks.mitigation: Recording is assigned only to the single worker task with an explicit 'exactly one' acceptance criterion; the planner records none.

decisions.title: Word definition
decisions.decision: In wrap, truncate and countWords a word is a maximal run of non-whitespace characters (/\S+/g).
